nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, exactly $n - 2$ of the positions $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ satisfy $i + 2 < n$, where $n - 2$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $n < 2$).
nodes.title: Number of positions with two successors

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. A position $i$ is a double ascent of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i+1) < \sigma(i+2)$.
nodes.title: Double ascent of a permutation

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. A position $i$ is a double descent of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) > \sigma(i+1) > \sigma(i+2)$.
nodes.title: Double descent of a permutation

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. A position $i$ is a peak of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i+1) > \sigma(i+2)$. Thus the peak entry is $\sigma(i+1)$, and the position recorded is $i$, that of the first of the three entries.
nodes.title: Peak of a permutation

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. A position $i$ is a valley of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) > \sigma(i+1) < \sigma(i+2)$. Thus the valley entry is $\sigma(i+1)$, and the position recorded is $i$, that of the first of the three entries.
nodes.title: Valley of a permutation

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i$ be a position. If $i + 2 < n$, then $i$ is exactly one of a double ascent, a double descent, a peak or a valley of $\sigma$; otherwise $i$ is none of them. That is, the number of these four properties that $i$ has is $1$ when $i + 2 < n$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Local shape of a position in a permutation

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and write $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{pk}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{vl}(\sigma)$ for its numbers of double ascents, double descents, peaks and valleys. Then $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma) + \mathrm{ddes}(\sigma) + \mathrm{pk}(\sigma) + \mathrm{vl}(\sigma) = n - 2$, where $n - 2$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $n < 2$).
nodes.title: Sum of the four local statistics of a permutation

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ that are double ascents of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Number of double ascents

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, $\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ that are double descents of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Number of double descents

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, $\mathrm{lmax}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such that $\sigma(j) < \sigma(i)$ for every position $j < i$, that is, the number of entries larger than every entry to their left.
nodes.title: Number of left-to-right maxima

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{lmin}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such that $\sigma(i) < \sigma(j)$ for every position $j < i$, that is, the number of entries smaller than every entry to their left.
nodes.title: Number of left-to-right minima

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{pk}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i + 1) > \sigma(i + 2)$, that is, the number of peaks of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Number of peaks of a permutation

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{rmax}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such that $\sigma(j) < \sigma(i)$ for every position $j > i$, that is, the number of entries larger than every entry to their right.
nodes.title: Number of right-to-left maxima

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{rmin}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such that $\sigma(i) < \sigma(j)$ for every position $j > i$, that is, the number of entries smaller than every entry to their right.
nodes.title: Number of right-to-left minima

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{vl}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) > \sigma(i + 1) < \sigma(i + 2)$, that is, the number of valleys of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Number of valleys of a permutation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
